newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST-New Zealand newspapers-Oct 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-New Zealand newspapers-Oct 7.

text.p: Labour and its likely allies, New Zealand First and the Alliance, have a 20-point lead over National in the latest opinion poll, sending National into the last week of the election campaign as the underdog.
National's party vote has fallen by six percent to 34 percent, while Labour's support rose six points to 24 percent, according to the latest One Network News-Colmar Brunton poll, aired last night.
Alliance had 15 percent support and New Zealand First 15 percent. Together, the opposition parties had 54 percent of the vote against National's 34 percent. Page 1.

Ngai Tahu chairman Charlie Crofts wept as he signed the Maori tribe's $170 million settlement with the government. The agreement ended a 150-year campaign by the South Island tribe for recognition that it had suffered through Crown actions. Page 1.

Despite Prime Minister Jim Bolger's efforts to turn tonight's final television leaders' debate wormless, performances in the debate will again be judged by a wiggly line that goes up when a select group of undecided voters like what they see and down when they don't. Page 1.

Labour leader Helen Clark has smoothed over ructions with former leader David Lange after his comments on Australian television that opposition MPs would be induced to defect to National after the election. Clark says Lange will "most certainly" be part of the party's campaign in its last week.

Maori voters, traditionally Labour supporters, have shifted their vote heavily from Labour to New Zealand First, according to a poll aired on Television New Zealand's Marae programme. The nationwide poll of 650 Maori voters showed overwhelming support for NZ FIrst leader Winston Peters, with 61 percent of Maori roll voters choosing him as their preferred prime minister. Page 2.
A group of National Party activists opposed to any coalition with the Christian parties has hit out with an "information kit" intended to discredit them. Page 2.

Shareholders of Irish Independent Newspapers gave the green light to a takeover bid for New Zealand's Wilson and Horton group at a general meeting in Dublin at the weekend. The $1.03 billion move, announced on September 16, will start as scheduled tomorrow. If successful it will give Independent 100 percent ownership of Wilson and Horton, New Zealand's biggest publishing and printing company. Page 18.

Mercury Energy is taking UtiliCorp NZ to court over its shareholder agreement with WEL Energy, despite indicating it will make a special offer for the company's Power NZ shares. Mercury successfully prosecuted UtiliCorp for failing to disclose an agreement with several shareholders in Power NZ that gave it first right of refusal over the shares.
UtiliCorp subsequently disclosed a near identical agreement with Hamilton-based WEL Energy and it is that which Mercury wants tested in court. Page 19.
National MP John Banks has bluntly admitted that National will be "consigned to oblivion" unless ACT New Zealand manages to cross the five per cent threshold and win seats in Parliament.

The warning, on his final radio talkback show, follows two weekend polls which indicate that power is slipping away from National towards a centre-left government headed by Labour leader Helen Clark. Page 1.

Labour leader Helen Clark and former prime minister David Lange have kissed and made up, blaming inaccurate radio reporting for their ill-tempered weekend. Lange at one point threatened to stop campaigning, but last night said he would continue to work for a Labour victory on Saturday.

Falsifying material to Inland Revenue or failure by tax specialists to disclose material would carry a maximum 30 years' imprisonment under a New Zealand First government if revenue involved was over $6 million.

National's discomfort with the Christian Coalition has led senior minister Jenny Shipley to challenge the Christians to make crystal clear whether they want abortion and sex education to be part of a coalition agreement.
